subject: error in formula with "generic0" to fit an "animal model" (genetics)

messages.author: 9ea95ff2561a8857
messages.subject: error in formula with "generic0" to fit an "animal model" (genetics)
parts:
Hello,
first of all, thanks a lot for providing INLA!

I would like to understand how to fit an "animal model" (a kind of linear mixed model, used in genetics) with INLA similar to what is done by AnimalINLA. (That is, I don't want to simply use the function from the AnimalINLA package.)

Here is the model specification:
y = W a + Z u  + e with e ~ N(0, sigma^2 I)
where y is Nx1, W is NxP, a is Px1 ("fixed effects", for instance several years), Z is NxQ, u is Qx1 ("random effects", for instance various plant varieties) and e is Nx1.
Moreover, the prior on u is N(0, sigma_u^2 A) where A is a known QxQ matrix.

I simulated data to end up with a data frame named "dat" with N=300 rows (P=3, Q=100) and 3 columns:
dat$year: factor with 3 levels
dat$animal: factor with 100 levels
dat$response: numeric

By reading INLA's documentation as well as AnimalINLA's code, here is the line I came up with to fit the model:

fit <- inla(formula=response ~ 1 +
                f(year, model="iid", constr=TRUE, hyper=list(theta=list(initial=-10, fixed=TRUE))) +
                f(animal, model="generic0", constr=TRUE, hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.5, 0.5), fixed=FALSE)), Cmatrix=solve(A)),
              family="gaussian",
              data=dat,
              verbose=TRUE, silent=TRUE)

However, here is the message I get:

    Error in inla(formula = response ~ 1 + f(year, model = "iid", constr = TRUE, :
       In f(animal): 'covariate' must match 'values', and both must either be 'numeric' , or 'factor'/'character'.

In this message, I don't understand what "covariate" and "values" refer to. Thanks in advance for any help!
Tim

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] error in formula with "generic0" to fit an "animal model" (genetics)
parts:
On Sun, 2015-07-26 at 10:48 -0700, Timothée Flutre wrote:

> However, here is the message I get:
>
> Error in inla(formula = response ~ 1 + f(year, model = "iid",
> constr = TRUE, :
> In f(animal): 'covariate' must match 'values', and both must
> either be 'numeric' , or 'factor'/'character'.

Hi,

the phrase 'covariate' is 'idx' in

... + f(idx, ...)

and for model 'generic0' these values must be 1, 2, ...., n where n is
the dimension of the precision matrix. (its the default value of the
argument 'values'). what you input is not like this, hence the error
message.

you can override this using the argument 'values' as shown here

> C = diag(3)
> r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx, model="generic", Cmatrix = Q), data =
data.frame(idx=1,y=0))
> r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx, model="generic", Cmatrix = Q), data =
data.frame(idx="a",y=0))
Error in inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx, model = "generic", Cmatrix = Q), data =
data.frame(idx = "a", :
In f(idx): 'covariate' must match 'values', and both must either be

> r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx, model="generic", Cmatrix = C, values=c("a",
"b", "c")), data = data.frame(idx="a",y=0))
>



Håvard
